cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

details: dependencykfeg 2.1.3, 25.0.3, 25.1.3 and 25.1.9 are part of one campaign that sends information about the installing machine to Burp Collaborator (oastify.com) out-of-band interaction hosts. 2.1.3 performs a DNS lookup of `94bp9h8fte9kz9v8btc6in8qnht8h85x.oastify.com` from its entry point `index.js`, so every `require` of the package signals the collector. 25.0.3, 25.1.3 and 25.1.9 contain no functionality of their own (the entry point exports an empty object or is missing) and declare a single dependency (`node-acct-utils`, aliased `node-acct-utilssss21` in 25.1.3 and 25.1.9) that is not fetched from the npm registry but from a tarball on GitHub, `https://github.com/GamerD11/ping_test/raw/refs/heads/main/node-acct-utils-1.0.0.tgz`. The code that runs at install time is therefore not part of the published packages, and the publisher replaced it on 2026-10-29 at 22:01 UTC. Both observed versions of that tarball run `node index.js` as a `preinstall` script and silently ignore errors. The first (tarball sha256 af59a1f75fb309422693a656404504c4ab7c25d31a70bf0c36cf2454dea35f43) is lightly obfuscated: it runs `whoami` and `hostname`, reads the working directory, home directory, platform, CPU architecture and Node.js version, and sends them as JSON tagged with the package name in an HTTP POST to `http://yrtew6v4g3w9myixyizv5cvfa6gx4zso.oastify.com/`. The second (tarball sha256 2707f1c7c853cd703495678ade5e3819a98620f5f6b6ca247b962d727b3ff84a) reads the collector host name at run time from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GamerD11/ping_test/main/burp_collaborator.txt` (at the time of writing `378jcbb9w8ce23y2enf0lhbkqbw2k58u.oastify.com`), queries `https://ipinfo.io/json` for the machine's public IP address, network operator and ASN, and sends those together with the username, hostname, home directory, working directory, platform, architecture and Node.js version in an HTTPS POST to that host with TLS certificate verification disabled; it tags the data with the name `claims-acct-unl`. The second stage is hosted in the GitHub repository `GamerD11/ping_test` (https://github.com/GamerD11/ping_test), created on 2026-10-29, which contains nothing but the payload tarball and `burp_collaborator.txt`; its owner controls the code that runs at install time. Because the second stage is fetched from a mutable GitHub URL, installing 25.0.3, 25.1.3 or 25.1.9 runs whatever the publisher currently hosts there. Impact: any developer or CI machine that installed one of these versions has disclosed its username, hostname, filesystem layout and (with the current second stage) its public network location to a third party. Remediation: remove the package, install with `--ignore-scripts` where possible, reject dependencies resolved from URLs outside the registry, and block oastify.com on build hosts. The `0.0.0-stage` version is an inert placeholder and 1.5.6 only performs a DNS lookup of the hex-encoded working directory under `google.com` from a `preinstall` script; neither is listed.

files.note: 2.1.3 entry point: DNS lookup of the oastify.com collector on require
25.0.3: declares node-acct-utils from the GitHub tarball URL
25.1.3: declares node-acct-utilssss21 from the GitHub tarball URL
25.1.9: declares node-acct-utilssss21 from the GitHub tarball URL
second stage v1 (served until 2026-10-29 22:01 UTC): preinstall, HTTP POST of username, hostname and paths to yrtew6v4g3w9myixyizv5cvfa6gx4zso.oastify.com
second stage v2 (current): preinstall, reads collector host from burp_collaborator.txt, ipinfo.io lookup, HTTPS POST of user, host, paths and public IP
